output.summary: Generic public plan for the private-app dogfood run (detailed plan kept in the root's private journal): the default graph with the root holding implement, nine phases from install to an engine-driven release whose deploying steps stay outside the engine with separate owner approvals, acceptance checks A1-A17, and owner decisions OD1-OD7 with identifying words redacted. Every public write by root or workers is scanned against a private deny-pattern list; later-release goals are migrated held; G1036 depends on G1037.

spec:
The owner's direction (2026-11-01), verbatim: "whitepaper should be after dogfood run, we'll use the [private app, name redacted] repository as a dogfood test - migrate the goals and execute through to a release."

Dogfood the Release 1 engine end to end on the owner's private web application repository (its location is in the root's private notes), which still has a pre-reset ZzzOps installation (.zzzops/PROJECT.md, POLICY.json, proposals, portfolio caches) and old-style goal issues:
1. Install the plugin built from this repository's dev in both Claude Code and Codex (the owner: "We can update Codex for the dogfooding rather than wait for release"; Codex moves off the 15b59a5 copies at the start of this run, and both harnesses take part). Legacy detection (G1015) must show the migrate item; run the migrate-zzzops-repository skill and bootstrap: capture the private app's intent with the owner, write policy from the templates (the Release 1 consolidated graph, G1022), the template provenance record (G1024), required capabilities (G1027) and the branching block (G1025).
2. Migrate the private app's open goals into goal branches; close or record the ones that no longer apply, with the owner.
3. Execute through to a release: run the migrated goals through the default graph (design with owner questions raised by review (G1026), reviews, approvals, base, tests, implementation, CI, integrate, merge), including at least one stacked dependent and one goal that restacks after its dependency merges; then cut the release branch when every goal of the release is done, sync it to dev, and finish it into the production branch (G1025). Deploys, tags and CI stay the private app's own; the owner approves the finish because it may deploy.
4. Exercise the failure paths that occur naturally or that the root can trigger safely: a review finding that reopens its target, a failing check, an expired lease reclaimed from a second clone, a policy branch that pauses work.

Acceptance:
- Every migrated goal closes done (or is closed with the owner's reason) with no hand edits of zzzops/** refs beyond REPAIR.md recipes.
- One the private app release is cut, synced and finished through the engine.
- Every defect found is captured as its own goal in this repository, and the run's notes (what worked, what did not, cost per goal) are written up for the whitepaper (G1002).
- Re-score the consolidated review lenses on these real goals (G1022's follow-up).


Replaces G1003 and G1035, whose branches were deleted to remove private details of the owner's dogfood app (owner decision, 2026-11-01). Anonymity rule (owner): "Anonymised entirely"; nothing in this repository names the app. The detailed run plan and every app-specific fact live in the root's private journal outside this repository; this goal's public artifacts (design, reviews, summaries, findings, responses, owner quotes, commit messages, PR text, defect goals) describe only the generic plan and are scanned against the journal's deny-pattern list before every write.
title: Dogfood Release 1 on a private web app repository: migrate its goals and execute through to a release
